migrationCompatibility.notes: upgrade() is untouched. Only downgrade() changes, and only in how it handles one error it cannot prevent. Production never runs downgrade, so deployed behaviour is identical; the blast radius is CI and local development.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: redeploy the prior release. Reverting this change restores the abort, which returns full-regression to 7 failures and 12 errors and puts #1402 back to red.

acceptanceCommands: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost:5432/<throwaway> PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests -m 'not live and not demo_contract' -q
doNotInfer: Do not force-drop juli_app to make the downgrade 'clean'. It is cluster-wide; another database in the cluster may still depend on it, and this migration cannot see that.

Do not assert only that the downgrade raised no exception. The pre-fix failure mode WAS silent — one transaction, rolled back, database left at head, caller believing it reached base. Assert alembic_version is empty.
Do not try to reproduce this with a single database. It needs a sibling database in the same cluster; test_workflow_runs_schema.py alone is 14/14 and the three failing files together are 31/31.
Do not 'fix' the schema tests that fail downstream. They are correct; they were reading a database that had silently rolled back to head.
Do not extend DROP OWNED BY and expect it to reach the sibling database. It covers the current database plus SHARED objects only — never another database's tables.
